findings.reason: clause (1) admits non-convergence as a completed outcome ("the pass its update stopped falling"), so a run where zero cases converge satisfies the whole done-when with the control fired on nothing; the plan's own §9 record (docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/fit-iteration-stored-cases-from-main.html) shipped exactly that state ("no case converged, so each row records why the section 2 bands could not be evaluated: … not judged: the fit did not converge, so no band reads it"), and the same record shows MAST-U's reconstructed current already at 2.28 %, outside the 1.5 % band before any perturbation, so the control there could never show the perturbation moved it.

findings.reason: 1,350 s x 400 slices is 540,000 s ≈ 150 card-hours, not 30, and the record §7 landed for this states "Four hundred converged slices would therefore cost roughly 120 P100 card-hours" at 1,111.7–1,193.3 s per slice on a P100, so the sentence contradicts both its own arithmetic and the cited measurement on the device and the total.
findings.text: §11's cost premise reads "about 1,350 s for 49 passes per slice on an H200, about 30 card-hours for one converged 400-slice arm"

findings.reason: the section's own opening states the MAST and ITER known states converge in one pass, so for two of the three §1 states there is no pass to reduce by a factor and the clause cannot be met as written on every previously-converged case; the clause needs a per-case statement (or an explicit exclusion of one-pass cases) before a node can be judged against it.
findings.text: §11 clause (2) requires "One change to the iteration reduces the passes to tolerance by a stated factor on every case that converged before, loses none of them"
